title: Sideby — Switch Mac desktops across multiple displays
description: Connect the Spaces already open on your Mac and switch displays together. See app and window titles above the connection table, then drag to adjust only what changed. No separate save step.
intro: Connect the Spaces that should move together. When things change, see what is open in Settings and drag to adjust the cells you need. No names or separate saves required.
requirements: macOS 14+ · Apple silicon · Free & open source
film_alt: Sideby switches three displays together, creates a connection by dragging a Space, and shows moving, swapping, and Option-copying cells.
film_note: Sideby 1.0.0 · 22.5-second motion graphic with fictional data, not a switching benchmark.
benefit_label: Spend less time switching each display
benefit_title: Keep the Spaces you already use.
benefit_text: An editor on your MacBook, a browser on your external display. Pair their desktops and move your displays together with your usual gesture.
benefits: See Spaces by display and their connections together.
Drop into the blank column to create a connection.
Drag to move, Option-drag to copy, and undo mistakes.
how_title: Start with the Spaces you need.
how_intro: Allow access, then choose Spaces in the empty cells. Start with just one connection.
steps: Check Accessibility and Screen Switching access in the guide.
Connect Spaces you want to see together in the same column. You can also start with Connect in current order. This does not switch your screens.
See your Spaces in Settings and drag to a cell for the same display. Changes are remembered immediately.
matrix_text: Edit cells directly in the menu. Hold ⌥⇧Space and click anywhere in a column to switch together. Choose Edit connections to see Space cards above the table. Drag to a cell for the same display, or click the card and then the cell. Settings uses the same editing flow. Filled cards show connected Spaces; dashed + cells are available for a connection. Use Move together to switch while editing.
matrix_alt: Actual app with distinct connected cards, dashed empty cells, and labelled Move together buttons.
matrix_note: Actual app views with fictional sample data.
small_features: Switch between the desktops on your MacBook, or include an external display when you connect it.
If other Spaces are added and positions shift, Sideby follows the connected Space. If it disappears, Sideby asks you to choose again. Connections for unplugged displays are kept.
A native menu-bar app with keyboard shortcuts and an interface that follows light and dark appearance.
faqs: The existing desktops that should switch together across your displays. Connections stay on your Mac and can be edited directly without naming or saving separate setups.
Does it create desktops or launch apps?
Sideby connects and switches existing Spaces. It does not create or delete desktops, launch or full-screen apps, or restore window positions.
What happens when I disconnect a display?
Its connections are kept. Use Show disconnected displays to inspect them, then reconnect the display when needed.
The current download supports Apple silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later. Download the DMG, move Sideby to Applications, and follow the first-run guide.

Accessibility supports configured global gestures and available app or window-title suggestions. Screen Switching access enables desktop commands; some paths also require System Events Automation. Desktop discovery and switching do not request Screen Recording permission.
Is it free, and where is my data stored?
Sideby is free and open source under MIT. Desktop connections and settings stay on your Mac. Sparkle updates require your approval to install.
end_text: See what is open. Adjust only the connections you need.
footer: Made for the way you already work.
onboarding_alt: The two-step guide shows Allow access and Connect desktops, with Connect in current order.
editor_text: Settings and the shortcut’s connection editor show each display’s Spaces above the table, with available app/window titles and the current Space. “Space · position 3” indicates list order, not a Mission Control desktop name. Even with no connections, drop a Space into an empty cell to create your first one. Drag between cells for the same display to move or swap. Hold ⌥ Option when dropping to copy. Clear one cell or one display, or select several columns to remove together. Even after clearing all connections, you can start again immediately. Undo keeps the last 20 connection changes, including after restarting Sideby.
editor_note: Changes are remembered immediately. Undo the last change with the Undo button or ⌘Z. No separate editor or Save changes step is needed.
editor_alt: Settings shows desktop contents and the connection table in the same window.
editor_overview: What if desktops or displays change?
editor_overview_text: Find new desktops in the upper list and connect them. If a desktop disappears, choose again in the affected cell. Sideby never replaces it with a different desktop at the same position. Disconnected displays keep their connections.
